notes: C4's error status is serialized inside the mixed DMI response word before reaching jtag_tdo_o; the response-word and shift-register elements are therefore treated as paths to the serial boundary output.

points.reason: The synchronized TMS sample controls the TAP command path, so changing or holding jtag_tms_i can select an unintended transition or prevent progress.
This wire carries the sampled TMS command into the TAP state conditions, where an altered value can steer or hold the TAP state.
The TMS condition selects every TAP state transition, including transitions into reset, pause, capture, shift and update states.
The synchronized JTAG data stream contains the DMI operation bits, so changing it can issue a different operation or prevent a valid operation.
This wire forwards the synchronized JTAG data bit into the DMI shift register, where the operation field is assembled.
The JTAG data bit shifts into tap_reg.dmi and its low operation bits later select whether dmi_ctrl.op becomes read, write or remains no-operation.
The controller assigns dmi_ctrl.op to no-operation by default and replaces it with the decoded DMI operation, so alteration can change or suppress a request.
The DMI operation is released on dmi_req_o.op, where changing or withholding the request operation can alter or block the external DMI transaction.
dmi_ctrl.busy blocks acceptance while high and is cleared only on dmi_rsp_i.ack, so forcing or clearing it can overlap transactions or stall new requests.
dmi_ctrl.err is cleared or asserted by the reset and busy-command conditions, so changing those conditions can make the reported DMI error status incorrect.
The error bit is packed into the next DMI response word, so changing this response path changes the status later shifted to JTAG.
The response word is captured into tap_reg.dmi and selected for serial output, so register selection or shifting can alter which error status is returned.
